brief: Credit cracked this week as the rates selloff accelerated, IG100 spreads widened ~4.6bps with high-beta bonds decompressing fastest, and HY had its largest down day in 17 months (index +18bps, insurance +38.5bps). All-in IG yields near 5.95% (multi-year highs) make yield attractive even as spreads stay historically tight, so the income story now outweighs the spread-compression story. Rate volatility (MOVE broke 100, first time since May) is sidelining yield-based demand just as supply peaks: $42bn IG priced this week, YTD $1.82tn (+26% YoY), plus SoftBank's record $11.14bn HY deal funding its OpenAI investment and pending Paramount Skydance (~$32bn IG, ~$12.4bn HY) and Tesla's speculative inaugural IG deal. AI-linked credit is a distinct driver: single-name AI CDS volumes are up ~400% YoY, the liquid universe grew from ~4 to ~10-12 names, and AI-disruption fears hit Tech/Cable HY specifically. Positioning turned defensive: hedge funds added HY shorts and IG protection, real money sold IG into strength. Loans diverge technically, posting their best inflow in 19 months. Conclusion: heavier supply plus faster rate moves raises the bar for further credit tightening into October.
